members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer was started with tg.start_soon(), which returns before the task actually reaches a checkpoint. If a caller sent a message immediately after entering the transport context, it could race with post_writer not yet listening on write_stream, causing dropped messages/hangs. Both PRs fix this identically: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None]` parameter to post_writer and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context, so the caller can use `tg.start()` and block until post_writer is truly ready.

members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer was started with tg.start_soon(), which returns before the task actually reaches a checkpoint. If a caller sent a message immediately after entering the transport context, it could race with post_writer not yet listening on write_stream, causing dropped messages/hangs. Both PRs fix this identically: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None]` parameter to post_writer and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context, so the caller can use `tg.start()` and block until post_writer is truly ready.

members.cluster_pick_reason: Both patch the exact same lines in utils.py and session.py, so they will conflict on merge regardless of which lands first. #2777 additionally drops the redundant f'{e}' interpolation from the raised message (e.g. `raise OAuthRegistrationError("Invalid registration response") from e` instead of embedding str(e) in the message text), avoiding duplicate error detail now that `from e` already surfaces the original exception in the traceback/chain — a small but concrete correctness improvement over #2565's version, which keeps the f-string duplication. #2565's title ('12 remaining raise sites') implies it is a narrower follow-up patch, while #2777 ('all except handlers') claims broader coverage across the codebase; whichever is confirmed to cover the full set of remaining unchained raises with passing CI should be kept, and given the overlapping hunks shown here #2777's approach is the cleaner of the two on the shared sites.
